description: PM2 integration layer: the pure mapper and the Pm2Client — the only module that imports the pm2 package. Depends on FEAT-001 (types, events, state hub, error tracker). Implements connection + exponential-backoff reconnection, launchBus with the pinned four-channel event->MonitorEvents translation and field-path defense, the intentional-action FIFO token model, the single metrics poll loop that emits metrics:tick, and bounded log-tail reading. Grounded in design.md 'PM2 integration layer', the pinned bus packet contracts, the intentional-action token model, the metrics poll loop (MEDIUM-1), the restart-overlimit disjointness (MEDIUM-3), aggregate semantics, and the error-handling table.
steps: src/pm2/mapper.ts: pure mapProcess(raw): ProcessSnapshot producing the per-NAME aggregate (instances = instance count, cpu/memory summed/representative, pmId/pid = primary instance) with status mapped to ProcStatus. Bus-packet normalizer helpers using the field-path defense: ev = packet.event ?? packet.data?.event, proc = packet.process ?? packet.data?.process; normalize process:exception data via data.stack ?? data.message ?? String(data). Log a one-time warn on a name collision (same name, differing pm_id set in one list). Add src/pm2/mapper.test.ts with recorded pm2.list fixtures, both flat and nested packet layouts, a process:exception packet, and a collision case.

src/pm2/client.ts: Pm2Client implementing the design interface — start() (non-blocking connect + reconnect loop), stop() (disconnect + close bus + clear timers), isConnected(), list(), describe(name), control(action,name) targeting an existing process BY NAME (resolves name->pm_id(s); start=start-a-stopped-process, distinct from startNew), startNew(opts), readLogsTail(name,lines,opts). Wrap all pm2 callback APIs in promisify-style helpers. On disconnect, control short-circuits to {ok:false,code:'PM2_UNAVAILABLE'} without throwing; a pm2-side control error yields {ok:false,code:'PM2_ERROR'}.

In client.ts implement connection + reconnection: pm2.connect on start; on success setConnected(true), initial list(), launchBus; on failure or later disconnect/bus error enter an exponential-backoff loop (1s,2s,4s... cap 30s, +/-20% jitter) retrying indefinitely, first failure warn then subsequent debug, keeping pm2Connected=false. On reconnect re-list, re-attach bus, flip connected true, broadcast.

In client.ts subscribe launchBus to the four channels process:event, process:exception, log:err, log:out and translate per design: online/start -> transition online (no error); restart -> transition + error:captured level restart tagged intentional per token consumption; restart overlimit -> transition errored + error:captured level crash, driving errored ONLY and NOT incrementing the restart-window counter (MEDIUM-3); exit -> error:captured level crash only if no intentional token consumed; stop -> transition stopped, intentional-vs-unexpected via token; delete -> remove from snapshot map (no error); process:exception -> error:captured level crash (normalized message/stack); log:err -> split lines, each emits log:line level error AND feeds ErrorTracker level error; log:out -> split lines, each emits log:line level info (not an error).

In client.ts implement the intentional-action token model: per-process FIFO queue of IntentionToken {kind:'stop'|'restart'|'delete', expiresAt}. On a control call push one token per expected lifecycle event (one per running instance from the current snapshot.instances, fallback 1): stop=>N stop, delete=>N delete, restart/reload=>N restart; start/startNew push none. expiresAt = now + GRACE_MS where GRACE_MS = INTENTIONAL_ACTION_GRACE_MS + the process kill_timeout when describe exposes it. On a stop/exit event drop expired tokens then consume exactly one non-expired FIFO token if present (one token suppresses exactly one event); consuming a restart token marks the emitted restart error intentional:true, else intentional:false; no token => unexpected (crash for exit, eligible for unexpected-stop). Sweep on each consume and on a 30s janitor timer.

In client.ts implement the metrics poll loop (MEDIUM-1): a single setInterval(METRICS_SAMPLE_SEC) started once on first successful connect, cleared on stop(). Each tick calls list(); on transient error skip the tick (no event, debug log, keep last samples); on success call MonitorState.applyPm2List and emit exactly one metrics:tick carrying that ProcessSnapshot[].

In client.ts implement readLogsTail(name,lines,opts): resolve pm_out_log_path/pm_err_log_path via describe, read the trailing `lines` physical lines (bounded end-of-file read; lines clamped <=2000) of the selected stream file(s); tag err-file lines error and out-file lines info; for stream=all merge+sort by embedded/estimated ts (fallback read order); apply level filter then q filter (case-insensitive substring, /regex/ form treated as regex) in memory over that slice. Whole-history search is out of scope.

Add src/pm2/client.test.ts covering the token model with an injected clock and a fake pm2 + fake snapshot providing instances: one-token-per-instance consume, FIFO order, expiry, restart exit->online suppression (restart tagged intentional:true), unexpected stop with no token, and that restart overlimit does not increment the restart counter. Isolate pm2 behind an injectable adapter so the package's real daemon is never needed.
Fix any import/wiring so src builds; do NOT yet wire Pm2Client into src/index.ts beyond what compiles (full bootstrap is FEAT-004).
acceptance_criteria: npm run build compiles with ZERO TypeScript errors (pm2 and @types/node resolve).

npm test passes for src/pm2/mapper.test.ts and src/pm2/client.test.ts including both bus-packet layouts, the process:exception packet, the token model (one-per-instance/FIFO/expiry/restart-suppression), and restart-overlimit NOT counting toward restart-threshold.
control() short-circuits to PM2_UNAVAILABLE when disconnected and never throws; the reconnection loop uses capped backoff with jitter.
The poll loop emits exactly one metrics:tick per successful list and is the only place a metrics timer exists.
Pm2Client is the only module importing the pm2 package (mapper is pure, no I/O).
verification: Run: npm run build  — zero tsc strict errors.
Run: npm test  — mapper and client unit tests pass.
Confirm (grep is not verification; rely on tests) via the client.test.ts assertions that the token model and restart-overlimit disjointness behave as specified.
